question: A kite is flying at a height of 75 m, and the string makes an angle of 60˚ with the ground. What is the length of the string?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a 30°-60°-90° right-angled triangle, the sides opposite to these angles are in the ratio 1 : √3 : 2.

The side opposite to 60° (height of the kite) is given as 75 m.

√3 parts = 75 m ⇒ 1 part = 75 ÷ √3 = 25√3 m.

The hypotenuse (length of the string) corresponds to 2 parts.

Length = 2 × 25√3 = 50√3 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 50√3 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Height of the kite from the ground (Perpendicular, AB) = 75 m

Angle of elevation made by the string with the ground (θ) = 60&am
